primary.title: A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field
primary.author: James Clerk Maxwell
primary.rationale: This is Maxwell's seminal paper introducing his equations and the concept of electromagnetic waves, a foundational work in physics.

primary.title: Theory of Heat
primary.author: James Clerk Maxwell
primary.rationale: A comprehensive textbook that covers thermodynamics and statistical mechanics, reflecting his significant contributions to these fields.

primary.title: Matter and Motion
primary.author: James Clerk Maxwell
primary.rationale: This work provides an accessible introduction to classical mechanics and the fundamental concepts of physics, intended for a broader audience.

secondary.title: Maxwell's Demon: Entropy, Classical and Quantum Information, and Computing
secondary.author: Mark O. Scully and Hartmut L. Brand
secondary.rationale: This book explores the implications of Maxwell's thought experiments, particularly Maxwell's Demon, in the context of information theory and quantum mechanics.

secondary.title: James Clerk Maxwell: A Biography
secondary.author: Ivan Tolstoy
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive biography offering insights into Maxwell's life, scientific work, and intellectual context.

secondary.title: The Conceptual Development of Quantum Mechanics
secondary.author: Max Jammer
secondary.rationale: While slightly before 1976, this is a foundational scholarly work that extensively discusses Maxwell's role in the transition to quantum theory, particularly through his statistical mechanics.

suggestions.notes: The secondary source by Max Jammer is slightly older than the requested 1976 cutoff but is a highly regarded and relevant scholarly work for understanding Maxwell's influence on later physics.
